To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reliability of software can be characterized by a macroscopic variable that we call software entropy.

the volume of software is a function of the number of its components and their interrelationships; its pressure is a measure of its complexity; its temperature is a measure of the quality of its design, and its entropy is a measure of how efficiently it uses its available components.
the macroscopic attributes are the software size, complexity, and entropy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a macroscopic theory of software that is analogous to statistical mechanics.
the statistical mechanical characterization of software systems.
the macroscopic characterization of software systems and its relationship to software reliability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the software engineering discipline has matured to the point where it can be viewed as a branch of statistical mechanics.
software hardening is a necessary condition for software reliability.
the macroscopic characterization of software is the key to its reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the macroscopic characterization of software provides a basis for the unification of various software engineering approaches to improving software reliability and a framework for the development of a general theory of software reliability.
software hardening can be achieved by increasing the entropy of the system, which is the macroscopic attribute that is analogous to temperature in physical systems.

the macroscopic characterization of software systems, and their statistical mechanics, provides a framework for a new discipline, software thermodynamics, that can be used to unify and improve the state of software development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
software hardening is a statistical process, and that the statistical mechanics approach to software hardening is an effective way to improve software reliability.
, just as physical systems have a phase transition between solid and liquid, so too do software systems.
, in addition to the well-known benefits of hardening, it is also important to understand how the macroscopic properties of software systems are affected by the underlying microscopic variables.
